scenario.name: Microsoft Sysmon & Mandiant DFIR — WMI Permanent Event Subscription Persistence (EventID 19 / 20 / 21)
scenario.overview: Picture a clean city hospital ward with a red-cross triage check-in desk, curtained patient exam bays, a wall of labeled medicine cabinets, and rolling stainless-steel medical carts. Walking briskly past the hospital triage desk in a borrowed white lab coat, an intruder grabs a spare clipboard and wheels a rolling medical cart down the ward corridor. In this real-world scenario, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the hospital triage check-in desk in tiny disguised batches, then bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the patient chart & medicine cart. The head triage nurse checks the electronic shift roster at the nurse station and spots a lab-coat visitor who was never assigned to that hospital ward. In this scenario (T1546.003, Microsoft Sysmon & Mandiant DFIR, WMI Permanent Event Subscription Persistence (EventID 19 / 20 / 21)), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: wMI __EventFilter WQL Trigger Registration, then commandLineEventConsumer, then sYSTEM Payload Execution Under wmiprvse.exe. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering WMI __EventFilter WQL Trigger Registration, then CommandLineEventConsumer, then SYSTEM Payload Execution Under wmiprvse.exe, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 19 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: WMI __EventFilter WQL Trigger Registration (Sysmon EventID 19)
stages.subtitle: Persistence (T1546.003 - Windows Management Instrumentation Event Subscription)
stages.description: Walking briskly past the hospital triage desk in a borrowed white lab coat, an intruder grabs a spare clipboard and wheels a rolling medical cart down the ward corridor. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the hospital triage check-in desk in tiny disguised batches while everyday visitors and the triage nurse go about their routine. Using PowerShell Set-WmiInstance or mofcomp.exe, the attacker creates a permanent __EventFilter instance in the root\subscription CIM namespace with a WQL polling query (SELECT * FROM __InstanceModificationEvent WITHIN 60 WHERE TargetInstance ISA "Win32_PerfFormattedData_PerfOS_System"). Sysmon EventID 19 (WmiEventFilter activity detected) logs the exact Query and EventNamespace (logged in Sysmon Event 19 with EventID=19 , Sysmon WmiEventFilter, Namespace=root\subscription, FilterName=SCMUpdaterFilter, WqlQuery=SELECT * FROM __InstanceModificationEvent WITHIN 60 WHERE TargetInstance ISA Win32_PerfFormattedData_PerfOS_System so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes Set-WmiInstance -Namespace root\subscription -Class __EventFilter -Arguments @{Name="SCMUpdaterFilter"; EventNamespace="root\cimv2"; QueryLanguage="WQL"; Query="SELECT * FROM __InstanceModificationEvent WITHIN 60 WHERE TargetInstance ISA 'Win32_PerfFormattedData_PerfOS_System'"} (which Registers permanent WMI MOF class instances , __EventFilter WQL trigger, CommandLineEventConsumer payload, and __FilterToConsumerBinding link insid so that creates fileless, repository-backed SYSTEM persistence , T1546.003 during "WMI __EventFilter WQL Trigger Registration , Sysmon EventID 19" that runs outside normal Startup folders and Services lists, detectable via Sysmon EventID 19, 20, and 21 and WMI-Activity EventID 5861). Next, the follow-up artifact Sysmon EventID 19: Operation=Created EventNamespace=root\cimv2 Name=SCMUpdaterFilter runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Sysmon EventID 19: Operation=Created EventNamespace=root\cimv2 Name=SCMUpdaterFilter via Sys so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1546.003 during "WMI __EventFilter WQL Trigger Registration , Sysmon EventID 19" , Using PowerShell Set-WmiInstance or mofcomp while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). stages.title: Stage 2: CommandLineEventConsumer & __FilterToConsumerBinding Persistence in OBJECTS.DATA (Sysmon EventID 20 & 21)
stages.subtitle: Persistence (T1546.003 - CIM Repository OBJECTS.DATA Serialization)
stages.description: Because every nurse assumes someone pushing an official medical cart belongs on shift, the intruder pulls confidential patient charts and opens the medicine supply drawer. Here in Step 2 inside the hospital ward, the intruder leaves a hidden spare latch behind so they can walk back into the hospital ward later without disturbing the sealed clean-supply closet. The attacker creates a CommandLineEventConsumer specifying the payload command line (Sysmon EventID 20) and binds it to SCMUpdaterFilter via __FilterToConsumerBinding (Sysmon EventID 21 and WMI-Activity EventID 5861). Both objects are serialized into C:\Windows\System32\wbem\Repository\OBJECTS.DATA (logged in Sysmon Event 20 with EventID=20 , WmiEventConsumer / 21 , WmiConsumerToFilter / 5861 , WMI-Activity, ConsumerName=SCMUpdaterConsumer, DestinationCommand=powershell.exe -NoP -W Hidden -Enc JABjAD0..., DiskRepository=C:\Windows\System32\wbem\Repository\OBJECTS.DATA so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes Set-WmiInstance -Namespace root\subscription -Class CommandLineEventConsumer -Arguments @{Name="SCMUpdaterConsumer"; CommandLineTemplate="powershell.exe -NoP -W Hidden -Enc JABjAD0..."} (which Registers permanent WMI MOF class instances , __EventFilter WQL trigger, CommandLineEventConsumer payload, and __FilterToConsumerBinding link insid so that creates fileless, repository-backed SYSTEM persistence , T1546.003 during "CommandLineEventConsumer & __FilterToConsumerBinding Persistence in OBJECTS.DATA , Sysmon EventID 20 & 21" that runs outside normal Startup folders and Services lists, detectable via Sysmon EventID 19, 20, and 21 and WMI-Activity EventID 5861). Next, the follow-up artifact Set-WmiInstance -Namespace root\subscription -Class __FilterToConsumerBinding -Arguments @{Filter=$Filter; Consumer=$Consumer} runs (which Registers permanent WMI MOF class instances , __EventFilter WQL trigger, CommandLineEventConsumer payload, and __FilterToConsumerBinding link insid so that creates fileless, repository-backed SYSTEM persistence , T1546.003 during "CommandLineEventConsumer & __FilterToConsumerBinding Persistence in OBJECTS.DATA , Sysmon EventID 20 & 21" that runs outside normal Startup folders and Services lists, detectable via Sysmon EventID 19, 20, and 21 and WMI-Activity EventID 5861). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ CommandLineEventConsumer Destination="powershell.exe -NoP -W Hidden -Enc JABjAD0..." / ⇠#2 ACK 20) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Winmgmt / WMI Core Service), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 scrcons.exe / wmiprvse.exe).

stages.title: Stage 3: SYSTEM Payload Execution Under wmiprvse.exe / scrcons.exe Parentage (Sysmon EventID 1)
stages.subtitle: Execution (T1047 - Windows Management Instrumentation)
stages.description: Quietly photocopying records onto a hidden notepad while standing beside the exam bay, the intruder wheels the cart right back toward the elevator lobby. In this final step inside the hospital ward, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the patient chart & medicine cart until the nurse station chart audit catches the mismatch. When the WQL timer condition evaluates to true, the WMI Provider Host (wmiprvse.exe) or WMI Standard Event Consumer (scrcons.exe) spawns the configured CommandLineTemplate as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM, creating a telltale parent-child process anomaly in Sysmon EventID 1 (logged in Sysmon Event 1 with EventID=1 , Sysmon ProcessCreate, ParentImage=C:\Windows\System32\wbem\scrcons.exe, ChildImage=C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe, UserContext=NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes ParentImage: C:\Windows\System32\wbem\scrcons.exe (or wmiprvse.exe) (which invokes the Windows Management Instrumentation command-line interface , wmic.exe or DCOM/WinRM provider host , wmiprvse.exe to execute Win32_Proces so that executes lateral movement or local process creation , T1047 via the trusted WMI provider daemon , wmiprvse.exe during "SYSTEM Payload Execution Under wmiprvse.exe / scrcons.exe Parentage , Sysmon EventID 1" to decouple the child process parent PID from the attacker's session). Next, the follow-up artifact Image: C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe -NoP -W Hidden -Enc JABjAD0... runs (which invokes the Windows PowerShell host , powershell.exe with stealth and execution-policy bypass flags , such as -NoP, -NonI, -W Hidden, -Exec Bypass so that achieves fileless in-memory staging and execution , T1047 during "SYSTEM Payload Execution Under wmiprvse.exe / scrcons.exe Parentage , Sysmon EventID 1" without writing compiled binaries to disk, while generating PowerShell Operational EventID 4104 , ScriptBlock and 4103 , Module/Pipeline telemetry). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe -NoP -W Hidden -Enc JABjAD0... / ⇠#3 ACK 1) from Node ③ (#3 Winmgmt / WMI Core Service) to Node ④ (#4 OBJECTS.DATA CIM Repository), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 scrcons.exe / wmiprvse.exe).

steps.howItWorksInPractice: Under the hood, the observed step executes Set-WmiInstance -Namespace root\subscription -Class CommandLineEventConsumer -Arguments @{Name="SCMUpdaterConsumer"; CommandLineTemplate="powershell.exe -NoP -W Hidden -Enc JABjAD0..."} (which Registers permanent WMI MOF class instances , __EventFilter WQL trigger, CommandLineEventConsumer payload, and __FilterToConsumerBinding link insid so that creates fileless, repository-backed SYSTEM persistence , T1546.003 during "CommandLineEventConsumer & __FilterToConsumerBinding Persistence in OBJECTS.DATA , Sysmon EventID 20 & 21" that runs outside normal Startup folders and Services lists, detectable via Sysmon EventID 19, 20, and 21 and WMI-Activity EventID 5861). Next, the follow-up artifact Set-WmiInstance -Namespace root\subscription -Class __FilterToConsumerBinding -Arguments @{Filter=$Filter; Consumer=$Consumer} runs (which Registers permanent WMI MOF class instances , __EventFilter WQL trigger, CommandLineEventConsumer payload, and __FilterToConsumerBinding link insid so that creates fileless, repository-backed SYSTEM persistence , T1546.003 during "CommandLineEventConsumer & __FilterToConsumerBinding Persistence in OBJECTS.DATA , Sysmon EventID 20 & 21" that runs outside normal Startup folders and Services lists, detectable via Sysmon EventID 19, 20, and 21 and WMI-Activity EventID 5861).

steps.plainTitle: SYSTEM Payload Execution Under wmiprvse.exe / scrcons.exe Parentage (Sysmon EventID 1)
steps.storyAnalogy: Quietly photocopying records onto a hidden notepad while standing beside the exam bay, the intruder wheels the cart right back toward the elevator lobby. In this final step inside the hospital ward, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the patient chart & medicine cart until the nurse station chart audit catches the mismatch.
steps.simpleExplanation: When the WQL timer condition evaluates to true, the WMI Provider Host (wmiprvse.exe) or WMI Standard Event Consumer (scrcons.exe) spawns the configured CommandLineTemplate as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM, creating a telltale parent-child process anomaly in Sysmon EventID 1 (logged in Sysmon Event 1 with EventID=1 , Sysmon ProcessCreate, ParentImage=C:\Windows\System32\wbem\scrcons.exe, ChildImage=C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe, UserContext=NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Under the hood, the observed step executes ParentImage: C:\Windows\System32\wbem\scrcons.exe (or wmiprvse.exe) (which invokes the Windows Management Instrumentation command-line interface , wmic.exe or DCOM/WinRM provider host , wmiprvse.exe to execute Win32_Proces so that executes lateral movement or local process creation , T1047 via the trusted WMI provider daemon , wmiprvse.exe during "SYSTEM Payload Execution Under wmiprvse.exe / scrcons.exe Parentage , Sysmon EventID 1" to decouple the child process parent PID from the attacker's session). Next, the follow-up artifact Image: C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe -NoP -W Hidden -Enc JABjAD0... runs (which invokes the Windows PowerShell host , powershell.exe with stealth and execution-policy bypass flags , such as -NoP, -NonI, -W Hidden, -Exec Bypass so that achieves fileless in-memory staging and execution , T1047 during "SYSTEM Payload Execution Under wmiprvse.exe / scrcons.exe Parentage , Sysmon EventID 1" without writing compiled binaries to disk, while generating PowerShell Operational EventID 4104 , ScriptBlock and 4103 , Module/Pipeline telemetry).
steps.diagramAlignment: On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 across the topology from Elevated PowerShell Session and Winmgmt / WMI Core Service toward OBJECTS.DATA CIM Repository and Sysmon EID 19/20/21 & WMI Log.
steps.detectionAndEvidence: Documented in Sysmon Event 1 (recording EventID=1 , Sysmon ProcessCreate, ParentImage=C:\Windows\System32\wbem\scrcons.exe, ChildImage=C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe, UserContext=NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM under T1047): Alert on any child process (powershell.exe, cmd.exe, mshta.exe, wscript.exe, rundll32.exe) spawned by C:\Windows\System32\wbem\scrcons.exe.
